instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about hard work and explain its meaning.
output: కష్టే ఫలి (Kashte phali) — 'Hard work bears fruit.' It means success comes only through sincere effort; there are no shortcuts.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about jealousy or wanting what others have.
output: దూరపు కొండలు నునుపు (Doorapu kondalu nunupu) — 'Distant hills look smooth.' It means other people's lives look perfect from far away, but every life has its rough edges.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about hunger.
output: ఆకలి రుచి ఎరుగదు (Aakali ruchi erugadu) — 'Hunger knows no taste.' When you are truly hungry, even simple food tastes delicious.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about parents loving their children.
output: కాకి పిల్ల కాకికి ముద్దు (Kaaki pilla kaakiki muddu) — "A crow's chick is dear to the crow." Every parent finds their own child beautiful, no matter what others think.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about speaking kindly.
output: నోరు మంచిదైతే ఊరు మంచిది (Noru manchidaite ooru manchidi) — 'If your words are good, the town is good to you.' Speak kindly and people will treat you kindly in return.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about excess.
output: అతి సర్వత్ర వర్జయేత్ (Ati sarvatra varjayet) — 'Avoid excess in everything.' Too much of anything — even a good thing — becomes harmful.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about wasted advice.
output: చెవిటి వాని ముందు శంఖం ఊదినట్లు (Cheviti vaani mundu shankham oodinatlu) — 'Like blowing a conch before a deaf man.' Giving advice to someone who refuses to listen is a waste of effort.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about being trapped in difficulty.
output: ముందు నుయ్యి వెనుక గొయ్యి (Mundu nuyyi venuka goyyi) — 'A well in front, a pit behind.' It describes being stuck with trouble on every side.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about fooling yourself.
output: పిల్లి కళ్ళు మూసుకుని పాలు తాగినట్లు (Pilli kallu moosukuni paalu taaginatlu) — 'Like a cat drinking milk with its eyes closed.' It means fooling yourself into thinking nobody notices your actions.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about big responsibilities.
output: ఎంత చెట్టుకు అంత గాలి (Enta chettuku anta gaali) — 'Each tree faces wind matching its size.' Bigger positions and bigger success bring bigger problems.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about human nature never changing.
output: కుక్క తోక వంకర (Kukka thoka vankara) — "A dog's tail stays crooked." Some people's nature never changes, no matter how hard you try to straighten them.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about children learning from parents.
output: ఆవు చేను మేస్తే దూడ గట్టున మేస్తుందా (Aavu chenu meste duda gattuna mestunda) — 'If the cow grazes the crop, will the calf graze only the bund?' Children copy their parents' behavior — good or bad.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about appreciating fine things.
output: గాడిదకు ఏమి తెలుసు గంధపు వాసన (Gaadidaku emi telusu gandhapu vaasana) — 'What does a donkey know of sandalwood's fragrance?' Some people cannot recognize or appreciate the value of fine things.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about treating guests well.
output: అతిథి దేవో భవ (Atithi devo bhava) — 'The guest is god.' A guest should be welcomed and treated with the same reverence as a deity.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about blindly copying others.
output: పులిని చూసి నక్క వాత పెట్టుకున్నట్టు (Pulini choosi nakka vaata pettukunnatlu) — 'Like the jackal branding itself after watching the tiger.' Copying others without having their strength or capacity only brings harm to yourself.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about acting too late.
output: చేతులు కాలాక ఆకులు పట్టుకున్నట్టు (Chetulu kaalaaka aakulu pattukunnatlu) — 'Like clutching leaves after your hands are burnt.' Taking precautions after the damage is already done is useless.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about danger from within.
output: ఇంటి దొంగను ఈశ్వరుడైనా పట్టలేడు (Inti donganu eeshwarudainaa pattaledu) — 'Even God cannot catch a thief from inside the house.' The hardest threats to stop are the ones that come from within your own circle.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about quality over quantity.
output: గంగిగోవు పాలు గరిటెడైనా చాలు (Gangigovu paalu garitedainaa chaalu) — 'Even a ladle of the sacred cow's milk is enough.' A small amount of something excellent is worth more than plenty of the ordinary.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about reaping what you sow.
output: చేసుకున్నవారికి చేసుకున్నంత మహాదేవా (Chesukunna vaariki chesukunna-anta mahaadevaa) — 'Each receives according to their own deeds, O Mahadeva.' Your actions decide your fate; you harvest exactly what you plant.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about empty promises.
output: అరచేతిలో వైకుంఠం చూపించడం (Arachetilo vaikuntham choopinchadam) — 'Showing heaven in the palm of the hand.' Making grand, impossible promises just to win someone over.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about listening to elders.
output: పెద్దల మాట చద్ది మూట (Peddala maata chaddi moota) — "Elders' words are a bundle of packed cold rice." The advice of experienced elders nourishes and sustains you on life's journey.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about a protector becoming the threat.
output: కంచె చేను మేసినట్టు (Kanche chenu mesinatlu) — 'Like the fence itself grazing the crop.' The worst betrayal is when the one appointed to protect you is the one who harms you.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about being gullible.
output: ఎద్దు ఈనిందంటే దూడను కట్టేయమన్నట్టు (Eddu eenindante doodanu katteyamannatlu) — 'When told the ox has given birth, he said tie up the calf.' Believing absurd claims without a second thought shows foolish gullibility.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about living on someone else's name.
output: చెట్టు పేరు చెప్పుకుని కాయలు అమ్ముకున్నట్టు (Chettu peru cheppukuni kaayalu ammukunnatlu) — 'Like selling fruit by invoking the tree's name.' Taking credit or profit using someone else's reputation instead of your own merit.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about gratitude.
output: అన్నం పెట్టిన చేయి కరవకూడదు (Annam pettina cheyi karavakoodadu) — 'Do not bite the hand that feeds you.' Never harm the person who has helped and supported you.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about using opportunity in time.
output: దీపం ఉండగానే ఇల్లు చక్కబెట్టుకోవాలి (Deepam undagaane illu chakkabettukovaali) — 'Set the house in order while the lamp still burns.' Act while the opportunity and the resources are still available to you.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about true worth needing no show.
output: బంగారానికి తావి అక్కర్లేదు (Bangaaraaniki taavi akkarledu) — 'Gold needs no perfume.' Genuine quality speaks for itself and needs no decoration or advertising.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about helping the wicked.
output: పాముకు పాలు పోసినట్టు (Paamuku paalu posinatlu) — 'Like feeding milk to a snake.' Showing kindness to a wicked person only strengthens them to harm you later.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about ignoring petty criticism.
output: ఏనుగు పోతుంటే కుక్కలు మొరుగుతాయి (Enugu pothunte kukkalu morugutaayi) — 'Dogs bark as the elephant walks past.' Great people continue on their path, undisturbed by petty criticism.

instruction: Tell me a Telugu proverb about wasted effort.
output: నీటి మీద రాతలు (Neeti meeda raatalu) — 'Writing on water.' Effort spent on something that leaves no lasting trace is completely wasted.
